{
  "findings": [

      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Import Prisma before using it in the Salesforce client",
      "body": "The new credential update references `prisma`, but this file never imports or declares it. This fails TypeScript checking and, if emitted anyway, throws a ReferenceError after a successful token refresh, preventing Salesforce client initialization."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 97,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Persist the parsed Google tokens, not the safeParse result",
      "body": "`parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns `{ success: true, data: tokens }`, unlike the previous schema.parse call, which returned the tokens themselves. Saving that entire result as the credential key removes access_token, refresh_token, and expiry_date from the top level. The next GoogleCalendarService instance cannot parse the stored credential. This affects ordinary Google refreshes even when credential sharing is disabled; persist the result's data instead."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts",
      "line": 8,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Replace computed schema keys with actual token fields",
      "body": "`z.string().toString()` and `z.string().optional().toString()` both produce the literal property name `[object Object]`; they do not declare wildcard properties. The second declaration overwrites the first, and Zod strips all undeclared fields. Consequently, a sync response containing access_token, expires_in, and refresh_token loses its expiry and refresh token. Zoom then calculates a NaN expiry, while Office 365 cannot retain the refreshed expiry. Define and normalize the supported expiry fields explicitly and preserve the required token fields."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts",
      "line": 15,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "Normalize refresh responses before returning them to adapters",
      "body": "The sync branch returns a fetch Response, but the fallback branch returns whatever the provider callback returns. Google and both Zoho adapters expect a response with `.data`, while HubSpot expects a decoded token object with `.accessToken` and `.expiresIn`. A fetch Response has none of these properties, regardless of the JSON sent by the sync server. Enabling syncing therefore breaks refreshes for these integrations. Decode and adapt the sync response to a consistent contract, and update the callers accordingly."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts",
      "line": 25,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Do not replace an omitted refresh token with a dummy value",
      "body": "This fallback runs even when credential sharing is disabled. Office365CalendarService explicitly accepts refresh responses without a refresh_token and merges the parsed response over the existing credentials. Adding the literal `refresh_token` causes that merge to overwrite the real refresh token, so the next refresh fails and the user must reconnect. Leave omitted refresh tokens absent so callers can preserve the existing value."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 93,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Pass the user ID rather than the credential ID to token syncing",
      "body": "The third argument of refreshOAuthTokens is serialized as `calcomUserId`, but this call passes the credential record's ID. Those IDs are unrelated. The parent platform will either fail to find the user or return another user's Bigin token when the IDs happen to overlap. Carry credential.userId through to this method and use it for the sync request."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts",
      "line": 92,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "Send the actual Zoom app slug to the sync endpoint",
      "body": "This sends `zoomvideo` as appSlug, but Zoom credentials are created with appId `zoom`, and the webhook identifies apps by their stored slug. A parent platform using the same app identifiers for ingestion and refresh cannot resolve this request. Use `zoom` rather than the integration directory name."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 75,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Route Salesforce refreshes through the configured sync endpoint",
      "body": "The newly added Salesforce refresh unconditionally calls Salesforce directly instead of refreshOAuthTokens. With sharing enabled, a credential whose refresh token is managed by the parent platform cannot initialize this client, even if its current access token is valid: initialization immediately attempts a direct refresh using a missing or placeholder refresh token. Honor the same sync routing used by the other adapters and initialize the connection with the refreshed credentials."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts",
      "line": 8,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "security",
      "title": "Authenticate outbound credential-sync requests",
      "body": "The request asks the parent platform to return a user's access token using only a numeric user ID and app slug, with no authentication header or signature. The configured webhook secret is checked only on inbound requests. A normally authenticated parent endpoint will reject these requests; accepting them as implemented would expose users' third-party access tokens to anyone who can reach that endpoint and enumerate IDs. Include a configured authentication mechanism in the outbound request."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts",
      "line": 78,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Clear the invalid flag when replacing revoked credentials",
      "body": "The update path replaces only the key. Google, Zoom, and Webex mark credentials invalid after an invalid_grant response, so syncing fresh credentials after a user reconnects on the parent platform leaves the existing record marked invalid. The webhook reports success without restoring the integration. Reset invalid to false when accepting replacement credentials."
    }
  ]
}

findings.title: Import Prisma before using it in the Salesforce client
findings.body: The new credential update references `prisma`, but this file never imports or declares it. This fails TypeScript checking and, if emitted anyway, throws a ReferenceError after a successful token refresh, preventing Salesforce client initialization.

findings.title: Persist the parsed Google tokens, not the safeParse result
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns `{ success: true, data: tokens }`, unlike the previous schema.parse call, which returned the tokens themselves. Saving that entire result as the credential key removes access_token, refresh_token, and expiry_date from the top level. The next GoogleCalendarService instance cannot parse the stored credential. This affects ordinary Google refreshes even when credential sharing is disabled; persist the result's data instead.

findings.title: Replace computed schema keys with actual token fields
findings.body: `z.string().toString()` and `z.string().optional().toString()` both produce the literal property name `[object Object]`; they do not declare wildcard properties. The second declaration overwrites the first, and Zod strips all undeclared fields. Consequently, a sync response containing access_token, expires_in, and refresh_token loses its expiry and refresh token. Zoom then calculates a NaN expiry, while Office 365 cannot retain the refreshed expiry. Define and normalize the supported expiry fields explicitly and preserve the required token fields.

findings.title: Normalize refresh responses before returning them to adapters
findings.body: The sync branch returns a fetch Response, but the fallback branch returns whatever the provider callback returns. Google and both Zoho adapters expect a response with `.data`, while HubSpot expects a decoded token object with `.accessToken` and `.expiresIn`. A fetch Response has none of these properties, regardless of the JSON sent by the sync server. Enabling syncing therefore breaks refreshes for these integrations. Decode and adapt the sync response to a consistent contract, and update the callers accordingly.

findings.title: Do not replace an omitted refresh token with a dummy value
findings.body: This fallback runs even when credential sharing is disabled. Office365CalendarService explicitly accepts refresh responses without a refresh_token and merges the parsed response over the existing credentials. Adding the literal `refresh_token` causes that merge to overwrite the real refresh token, so the next refresh fails and the user must reconnect. Leave omitted refresh tokens absent so callers can preserve the existing value.

findings.title: Pass the user ID rather than the credential ID to token syncing
findings.body: The third argument of refreshOAuthTokens is serialized as `calcomUserId`, but this call passes the credential record's ID. Those IDs are unrelated. The parent platform will either fail to find the user or return another user's Bigin token when the IDs happen to overlap. Carry credential.userId through to this method and use it for the sync request.

findings.title: Send the actual Zoom app slug to the sync endpoint
findings.body: This sends `zoomvideo` as appSlug, but Zoom credentials are created with appId `zoom`, and the webhook identifies apps by their stored slug. A parent platform using the same app identifiers for ingestion and refresh cannot resolve this request. Use `zoom` rather than the integration directory name.

findings.title: Route Salesforce refreshes through the configured sync endpoint
findings.body: The newly added Salesforce refresh unconditionally calls Salesforce directly instead of refreshOAuthTokens. With sharing enabled, a credential whose refresh token is managed by the parent platform cannot initialize this client, even if its current access token is valid: initialization immediately attempts a direct refresh using a missing or placeholder refresh token. Honor the same sync routing used by the other adapters and initialize the connection with the refreshed credentials.

findings.body: The request asks the parent platform to return a user's access token using only a numeric user ID and app slug, with no authentication header or signature. The configured webhook secret is checked only on inbound requests. A normally authenticated parent endpoint will reject these requests; accepting them as implemented would expose users' third-party access tokens to anyone who can reach that endpoint and enumerate IDs. Include a configured authentication mechanism in the outbound request.

findings.title: Clear the invalid flag when replacing revoked credentials
findings.body: The update path replaces only the key. Google, Zoom, and Webex mark credentials invalid after an invalid_grant response, so syncing fresh credentials after a user reconnects on the parent platform leaves the existing record marked invalid. The webhook reports success without restoring the integration. Reset invalid to false when accepting replacement credentials.
